issues.legal_issue: A civil court lacks jurisdiction to decide a rival claim to a ryotwari patta after the dispute has been determined under a statutory process that makes the determination final.
material_facts: A dispute arose between rival claimants over entitlement to a ryotwari patta for land in an estate.

The Settlement Officer determined which claimant was entitled to the patta, and the civil suit later sought a declaration of title and possession based on conveyances while challenging the effect of that determination.
The governing enactment provided for determination of who was the lawful ryot and made the decision final, subject to an appeal to the Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit insofar as it challenged the determination of the rival claim to the ryotwari patta; the Settlement Officer’s decision was final and could not be questioned in court.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 56(1)(c) and section 56(2) of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, the Settlement Officer determines who is the lawful ryot, including in a dispute between rival claimants, and the decision is final unless appealed to the Tribunal, whose decision is likewise final and not open to challenge in court. The Court followed Muddada Chayanna v. Karnam Narayana, which approved the interpretation in T. Munuswami Naidu v. R. Venkata Reddi and held that the statutory authorities have exclusive jurisdiction over such disputes; it noted that Cherukuru Muthayya v. Gadde Gopalakrishnayya had been overruled.

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_pattta_entitlement: A party brought a civil suit seeking relief that requires the court to reconsider entitlement to a ryotwari patta.
predicates.statutory_process_decides_rival_ryot_cla: A statutory authority is empowered to decide which of competing claimants is the lawful ryot for the holding and has determined that dispute.
predicates.statutory_decision_is_final: The governing statutory process makes the authority’s decision, or the appellate authority’s decision, final and not challengeable in court.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges patta entitlement already determined through a statutory process whose decision is final, the civil court cannot review that entitlement.

issues.legal_issue: A law governing a territory before its transfer continues to apply there when the transfer preserves existing laws, and a later repeal by the former legislature does not displace that law in the transferred territory.
material_facts: The district containing the disputed lands was transferred from one state to another while the transfer legislation provided that existing laws would continue to apply in the transferred territory.
The enactment containing the provision making decisions on rival ryot claims final was in force in the district at the time of transfer.
The former state’s legislature later repealed that provision, but the transferred district formed part of the new state.
issues.conclusion: The provision remained in force in the transferred district, and its later repeal by the former state’s legislature was ineffective there.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53 of the Andhra State Act, 1953 preserved the laws in force in transferred territories until changed by a competent legislature or authority. Accordingly, section 56 of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, as in force on the transfer date, continued to apply in the district; its repeal by the Madras Legislature did not affect that territory. Krishnaswami Thevar v. Perumal Konar and A.R. Sanjeevi Naicker v. P.M. Shanmugham Udayar were distinguished because they concerned the law after section 56 had been repealed in Madras, and Pinninty Peda Govindayya v. Pinninty Subbarao was distinguished because it did not concern a comparable finality provision.

predicates.territory_transferred_with_existing_laws: A territory was transferred to a new state under an arrangement that continued the laws already applying there.
predicates.relevant_law_was_in_force_at_transfer: The law relevant to the dispute applied in the territory when the transfer took effect.
predicates.later_repeal_by_former_legislature: The legislature of the state from which the territory was transferred later repealed that law.

issues.definition: If a territory transfers with its existing laws preserved, a law then in force there remains applicable despite its later repeal by the former state’s legislature.
